name: Ray-marched Volumetric Fog
definition: A technique to simulate light absorption, scattering, soft shadows, and light shafts by treating fog as a 3D volume of participating media traced via ray-marching from the camera to the scene.
summary: Ray-marched volumetric fog simulates light absorption and scattering by tracing rays from the camera through a 3D volume, differing from backward methods by enabling early-out optimizations and operating as a full-screen post-process.
